title: Bind price rules through method handles

blocks.text: The shop's checkout applies price rules named in its config, such as `practice.Seasonal#winterSale`: a class and one of its public methods that takes a price in cents and returns the new price in cents. The checkout binds every rule once when it starts and then applies it to every basket, so the binding is where a wrong entry should be caught. Last month an entry named a method that returns an `int`, and it was accepted: baskets went through with prices cut to whole euros until someone noticed.
`PriceRules.bind` already creates the rule's object and wraps the call. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/PriceRules.java` with `java.lang.invoke` method handles:

items: `lookup(type, methodName)`: the handle for the rule method;

blocks.text: When you're done, a bound rule returns what its method returns for any price, and an entry whose method doesn't exist or doesn't take and return a price in cents is refused when it is bound, with an `IllegalArgumentException` that names the method. About seven lines in total.

cases.says: a bound rule returns what the named method returns, for prices beyond the int range too
the rule runs on the instance bind created, with that instance's state
a method name the class doesn't have is refused at bind time with IllegalArgumentException naming it
a method that takes a long but returns an int is refused at bind time, because the lookup includes the return type

origin.section: A Method Handle Has a Type, and invokeExact Holds the Call Site to It

concepts: findVirtual looks a method up by its full type, return type included, and a type that doesn't match fails at the lookup.
